pr.title: Leave a plan's account of merged work as it is
pr.head: 7e87740250ecaa5d614bf1b79aa07f8976c7b13d

summary: Projector keeps each project's plan in Git under docs/projects/, and project init writes a block of conventions into every adopting repository's AGENTS.md. That block told agents to "keep docs/ describing the behavior on the current branch". Because plans live under docs/, agents and the review loop read the rule as covering plans whose work had already merged. Review findings on later changes then asked agents to rewrite those plans, which cost review rounds and erased the record of what was decided.
This pull request says when a plan stops being a guide and becomes a record, and tells every agent that edits a plan or judges a finding about one to leave the record alone:

• A record is all of a completed plan, and each section of an unfinished plan whose behavior the default branch already has. Status alone cannot tell you which sections are records, because a plan can stay in-progress long after its first sections merge.
  • Later work that changes recorded behavior updates the living documentation instead. When that work belongs to the same project, it appends a numbered section that names the section it supersedes.
  • A record still changes through the project commands for status and priority, and when a renamed project's references are swept.
The change is all prose and one template, plus the hash that pins the template's new version. It changes no code path.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Plan: a project's readme.md under docs/projects/, with numbered sections that code and other documents cite.
  • Record: the part of a plan that describes work already merged into the default branch.
  • Living documentation: the rest of docs/, which always describes the current behavior.
  • Projector block: the generated section of AGENTS.md between projector:begin and projector:end, written from agents-block.md.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The Projector review of 7e87740 is clean, with one suggestion: name project owner among the ways a record still changes. The review also asks whether finish should say to record a deviation in an appended section.

groups.title: The generated block draws the line between plans and documentation
groups.kicker: The template, this repository's copy of it, and the hash that pins it
intro: The Projector block is the text project init writes into each adopting repository's AGENTS.md. Its template moves to version 15. The old sentence about keeping docs/ current now names the living documentation, and a new paragraph says that a plan is not living documentation and when its account of merged work becomes a record.

tests/test_instructions.py pins each version's template by hash, so the template cannot change without a version bump. This repository's own AGENTS.md is regenerated from the template, and project check would report it stale if the two differed.

checks.text: The AGENTS.md block is byte-identical to the template with {projects_dir} filled in as docs/projects, and the full test suite passes with the new hash.
Running project init on a temporary repository holding the version-14 block upgraded it to version 15 and kept the repository's own text above the block.

groups.title: The projects README says when a plan becomes a record
groups.kicker: The full rule for this repository, and one sentence of it for new adopters
intro: docs/projects/README.md is the reference for the project model. A new section, "Keep a plan as a record once its work merges", gives the rule in full: which parts of a plan are records, what later work does instead of editing them, and the two ways a record still changes.

project init writes project-readme.md as a new adopter's docs/projects/README.md, so that template gets the rule in one sentence. An existing adopter keeps the README it has, because init only creates the file when it is missing.

files.note: The new section placed after "Write a project plan".

checks.text: This list of the ways a record still changes leaves out project owner, which the README's frontmatter section uses to set the owner. The review lists that as a suggestion.

files.note: One sentence of the rule for the README that init creates.

groups.title: Each skill that edits a plan or judges a finding follows the rule
groups.kicker: The review method, fix-pr, implement, and spec
intro: The rule matters where an agent decides whether to edit a plan. Each of these skills now uses the same test for a record: a completed plan, or a section whose behavior the default branch already has.

• The review method drops a finding that asks a change to rewrite or annotate a record, even one that cites the rule that keeps docs/ current. When living documentation went stale, the finding asks for that document instead.
  • fix-pr declines such a finding with that reason, and fixes the living document when one describes the same behavior.
  • implement and spec append a section that names the one it supersedes, rather than rewriting a merged section, and leave other projects' records alone.
These are instructions a model follows, so no test exercises them. Read each paragraph for whether it says the same thing as the README.
